title: Introduce AZ-aware PrivateLink proxy + route-mapper for control-plane endpoints
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: private control-plane endpoints for on-prem/VPC customers must remain reachable during partial AZ failures and UX should avoid per-customer manual route-table surgery. This PR introduces an AZ-aware PrivateLink proxy (daemon + small control-plane component) and a route-mapper terraform module that automates deterministic ENI/interface-endpoint placement, per-AZ fallback, and safe DNS alias migration. The change touches three areas: terraform modules (new module vpc/controlplane-proxy), Helm chart (installer chart: add control-plane-proxy subchart and RBAC), and the installer migration script (idempotent migration path to convert existing interface endpoints to be fronted by the proxy and switch DNS aliases with TTL-drain). Key goals: 1) Provide graceful AZ failover without modifying customer application routing. 2) Keep endpoint ENI allocation deterministic so security groups can be applied predictably. 3) Enable staged rollout using feature flags and a safe rollback path. Design summary: the proxy runs in each AZ on a small EC2 or light-weight instancegroup and creates a single ENI per AZ that registers behind the interface endpoint via PrivateLink. The route-mapper terraform module ensures one subnet per AZ is used and claims the same ENI IP via a deterministic naming/tagging scheme. Health checks are performed by the proxy and the control plane updates Route53 private DNS aliases to point to healthy AZs with low TTL during migration windows. Compatibility: works with transit gateway and peered VPCs; includes explicit opt-out for customers that prefer direct interface endpoints. Rollout plan: 1) dry-run terraform apply that creates proxy infra but leaves DNS untouched; 2) enable proxy in a canary customer; 3) run migration script to atomically update Route53 aliases during low-traffic window; 4) monitor metrics (latency, 5xxs, endpoint accept-rate) and revert if needed. Rollback: migration script includes a --rollback token that reverts DNS aliases and tears down proxy ENIs created by the module. Security considerations: minimal IAM needed for the proxy to update Route53 aliases within the customer's zone (least privilege policy included), SG hardening template ensures control-plane ports are limited to known mgmt subnets. Testing: unit tests for terraform modules (plan assertions), helm unit tests (chart rendering), end-to-end canary in perf-lab with simulated AZ flaps. Backwards compatibility: existing customers not opting into the new module experience no changes. Documentation: installer README updated with migration steps, and an operator playbook added under docs/migrations/controlplane-proxy.md. Related work: replaces earlier manual endpoint failover runbooks and complements the egress allocator and conditional privatelink work.
